title: The Jazz Alley series and its guests
summary: The series Jazz Alley used Chicago men to back guests such as Barney Bigard and Pee Wee Russell. It was shown on 205 stations.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: So then we started doing Chicago things, and using Chicago men to back guests. So I used different people that would play. And brought in Barney Bigard and Doc Evans before he died. Pee Wee Russell was on before he died, Jimmy McPartland Eddie Condon before he died, Bud Freeman, besides J. C. Higginbothom and Parenti and people like that.
What was the name of that series?

Jazz Alley. And it was shown all over the country. 205 stations showed it. Now, the worst show I did in my estimation was the one with Eddie Condon and Tony Parenti, Smokey Starr, -- you mentioned this drummer, plays with a press roll.
Monty Monchoy, J.C. Higginbothom and myself. And the reason it was so bad, in my estimation, was because the fellows were so tired. They had come -- some of them had come from New York.
